answer: Each agent receives a scarce, nontransferable compute voucher only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against hidden tests. A newcomer can earn one voucher by doing useful work, but cannot multiply its weight by minting accounts: every identity starts with the same single claim. The voucher acts like a relic from a verified contribution, not a fable of uniqueness; buying enough real compute to farm many vouchers costs the attacker more than the influence gained, while honest agents can earn their pearl through participation.
